metadata.case_name: NG CHAI MAN AND ANOTHER v. LEUNG NGAN

plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: would have been able to work as an amah until the age of 70

injuries.description: fracture of the medial side of the upper end of the left tibia
source: sustained a fracture of the medial side of the upper end of the left tibia.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of upper end of tibia, medial condyle

injuries.description: permanent damage to the condyle of the tibia (front part of the lateral condyle slightly depressed downwards by one or two millimeters and a bony projection protrudes at the front of the tibia)
source: There was permanent damage to the condyle of the tibia, in that the front part of the lateral condyle is slightly depressed downwards by one or two millimeters and a bony projection protrudes at the front of the tibia.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of upper end of tibia, lateral condyle

injuries.description: osteoarthritis of the knee (predicted to develop)
source: Since the fracture involves the condyle, which is partially displaced and is a weight-bearing section of the surface of the knee joint, osteoarthritis would inevitably develop.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the knee or lower leg

manifestations.description: unable to walk as far as she could do before the accident
unable to stand for more than one or two hours at a time without pain and discomfort
impairment was assessed at 1% but would increase to 3-4% impairment by the age of 70
disabilities were permanent and would gradually worsen as osteoarthritis developed

treatments_received: plaster cast on her leg for six weeks
used a walking stick for a further two weeks
physiotherapy was offered but not accepted until a later date

losses.description: pain, suffering and loss of amenities (award of $18,000)
unable to walk as far as before the accident; unable to stand for more than one or two hours without pain; could no longer squat

comparable_cases.case_name: Wong Yuk Chau and Another v. Tang Suk Yee
